newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf Atochem agrees Chinese chemicals joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Elf Atochem agrees Chinese chemicals joint venture.

text.p: Elf Atochem, the chemicals unit of Elf Aquitaine, said on Tuesday it had agreed to a joint venture with China's Wuhan Organic Chemicals Industry Corp (WOCIC) to manufacture benzyl chloride and derivatives.
Elf Atochem would have a 60 percent stake in the new company, ATO WOCIC, and the remaining 40 percent would be held by WOCIC, Elf said in a statement. They planned investments of $20 million by 1999.

The joint venture will immediately take over the running of WOCIC's existing 12,000 tonnes per year benzyl chloride plant as well as a number of smaller benzyl chloride derivatives plants with total capacity of 3,000 tonnes per year.
By 1999, ATO WOCIC would have a 25,000 tonne per year manufacturing capacity for benzyl chloride, by hiking capacity at the existing plant, and a new 3,000 tonne per year phenylacetic acid plant.
Benzyl chloride is the raw material for phenylacetic acid as well as various solvents and plasticisers. Phenylacetic acid is used in the manufacture of a type of penicillin.
